biggest_catch: GreenPal's official vendor handbook confirms the payment flow — but the customer's card isn't charged until 48 hours after the job, so there is no same-day cashout.
catches: Official: customer has 48 hours to inspect and pay; card auto-charged 48h after completion if they do nothing.
Funds then move via your Stripe account on Stripe's payout schedule (yourgreenpal.com says Stripe controls holds and payout timing).
GreenPal takes a 5% platform fee; Stripe takes ~2.9% + $0.30.
You set your own bid prices — there is no official fixed per-job payout amount.
Requires your own equipment and business skills/licenses.

c1.evidence: GreenPal is a real lawn-care marketplace; official vendor handbook on yourgreenpal.com confirms the payment flow.

c2.evidence: No official fixed per-job amount — 'GreenPal gives its vendors the liberty to set their prices.' Official $50 example is illustrative only.

c4.evidence: Official: 48-hour inspection window before the card is charged — not same-day.

notes: Checked 2026-09-23. GreenPal is legitimate but fails this lane: vendor-set pricing (no concrete official amount) and 48h+ payout timing. Speed would be days regardless.
payout_quote: Meanwhile… Your customer will get an email letting them know they have 48 hours to check over your work... or if they do nothing (most GreenPal users), the system will charge your client's card on file automatically 48 hours later for you. (yourgreenpal.com)
payout_value_note: vendor-set bids, no official fixed amount

s5.note: Official handbook confirms timing — days, not today.

timing: Official: card charged 48h after completion; Stripe payout schedule after that.
